comparable_cases.why_comparable: Same address (1801 Haight St, 15m), same existing restaurant, approved Type 47 license transfer in May 2024. Agency referral for ABC Type 47 within the Haight Street Alcohol Restricted Use Subdistrict.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: Planning approved the current Type 47 as a continuation of existing use in the Haight RUSD, finding that prior Type 06/74 craft distillery licenses were similar to Type 47, so no CUA was required. This established that the restaurant's alcohol service is grandfathered, directly supporting the current outdoor expansion.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: Same address (1801 Haight St, 15m), approved CUA in 1992 to expand this non-conforming restaurant from 820 sq ft to 2,270 sq ft in the Haight Street NCD. Use decision by Planning Commission.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: The Commission approved a major expansion of this restaurant 33 years ago, establishing precedent that enlargement of an existing restaurant at this site is appropriate. The concept has operated continuously since, suggesting operational compatibility with the neighborhood.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: Outdoor dining for existing restaurant at 1650-1654 Haight St (230m west, same NCD-HAIGHT district). Required both CUA and Variance (separate case 2007.1046V). Use decisions approved January 2008.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: Outdoor dining on Haight Street required a Conditional Use Authorization (not just over-the-counter approval), taking 4 months from filing to CUA approval. The variance was filed 3 months after the CUA and approved 12 days later, suggesting technical rear-yard or setback issues common to this corridor.

comparable_cases.address: 1640 - 1640 HAIGHT ST GROUND, SAN FRANCISCO, CA 94117
comparable_cases.why_comparable: Outdoor seating for existing restaurant at 1640 Haight St (247m west, same NCD-HAIGHT district). Agency referral approved May 2013 as continuation of use under prior CUA cases.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: Planning permitted outdoor seating as a continuation of existing restaurant use citing prior CUA language (CU80.096 and 1988.341V), with the explicit condition that no building expansion or lightwell infill was allowed. This suggests outdoor seating tied to historical approvals may be handled administratively rather than requiring new CUA.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: Limited Live Performance permit with outdoor entertainment and amplified sound in a parklet at 1807 Haight St (24m away, same block, NCD-HAIGHT district). Entertainment Commission referral approved June 2024.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: Planning approved outdoor entertainment in a parklet at the bar next door just 8 months ago, confirming that outdoor use expansions on this block are currently viewed favorably. The proximity (24m) and recency are strong positive signals for outdoor dining at 1801.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: ABC Type 41 transfer for existing restaurant at 1790 Haight St (53m across the street, NCD-HAIGHT). Agency referral approved August 2022 for continuation of existing liquor establishment in Haight RUSD.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: Planning routinely approves ABC license transfers for existing restaurants in the Haight RUSD under the continuation-of-use exception (PC §781.9(c)(4)), even with eight on-sale licenses within 500 ft. Since this concept already holds a Type 47, outdoor expansion should not trigger new liquor-establishment review.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: Change of use from movie house to restaurant at 1721-1737 Haight St (68m east, NCD-HAIGHT). CUA approved October 2012 after 6-month review.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: A major change of use to restaurant on this corridor required CUA and took 6 months, but was approved, showing that the Commission supports restaurant density on Haight Street even in the NCD district.

filing_playbook.action: Schedule a pre-application meeting with San Francisco Planning to confirm whether the outdoor dining area meets all limits of Planning Code § 202.2(a)(7) or requires a Conditional Use Authorization.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Present the parking-lot location, proposed hours (request confirmation whether 9 a.m. to 10 p.m. is acceptable), seating plan (no standing areas), and alcohol service method (served by wait staff at tables only, not self-service). Ask whether this is a principally permitted outdoor activity area or requires CUA under § 178 as an enlargement. Request a written Letter of Determination or email confirmation before filing any applications.

filing_playbook.action: If Planning confirms a Conditional Use Authorization is required, prepare and file a CUA application with San Francisco Planning, including a project description, site plan, seating layout, hours of operation, alcohol service plan, and neighbor outreach documentation.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Frame the proposal as an enlargement of a long-established restaurant (operating since at least 1992, previously approved for expansion under case 1992.148C) that improves the outdoor dining character of Haight Street. Emphasize that the existing ABC Type 47 licence continues without establishing a new on-sale liquor establishment, consistent with Planning's May 2024 interpretation in case 2023-010501MIS. Commit to hours ending by 10 p.m., seated service only, and alcohol served by wait staff at tables. Highlight that the adjacent bar at 1807 Haight St was approved for outdoor entertainment in a parklet in June 2024, showing current Planning support for outdoor uses on this block.

filing_playbook.action: Submit building permit plans to the SF Department of Building Inspection for the tenant improvements (raised outdoor structure, new restroom, exit signage), with architectural plans stamped by a California-licensed architect.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Include the site plan showing the parking-lot outdoor dining area, structural details of any raised platform, restroom and exit upgrades, and confirmation that no building footprint expansion or rear-yard encroachment occurs. Request routing to Planning and DPH. Attach the Letter of Determination or CUA approval from step 1 or 2 to show zoning compliance for the outdoor area.

filing_playbook.action: Submit DPH plan check application for the kitchen and outdoor dining area through the SF Department of Public Health Environmental Health portal, including menu, equipment list, and finishes schedule.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Describe limited cooking (the concept states limited cooking type), the outdoor dining area as an extension of the existing restaurant, and any new handwash or prep sinks. Request a pre-final inspection at 80% construction completion and schedule the final pre-opening inspection at least two weeks in advance with the assigned plan reviewer.

timeline_cost.notes: This range is the time to approval if the Conditional Use Authorization and building permit are granted. It covers the CUA (120–300 days from filing to Commission approval per the 2007 outdoor dining case at 1650 Haight St and typical CUA timelines) and the building permit (14–120 days). The CUA is the critical path: pre-application meetings and preparation add 4–8 weeks before filing, environmental review and neighborhood notification add 60–90 days, and hearing scheduling takes another 30–60 days. If Planning determines at the pre-application meeting that the outdoor area is principally permitted under PC § 202.2(a)(7), the timeline drops to 14–120 days for the building permit and health permit only (submitted in parallel), and the cost drops to $800–$15,000 building permit plus $1,298–$3,500 health plan check and permit, totaling roughly $2,100–$18,500. The cost range shown assumes a CUA is required: approximately $3,100–$15,000 for a CUA (depending on construction valuation and fee waiver eligibility, based on catalog entry for sf.conditional_use_authorization) plus $800–$15,000 building permit, excluding the health permit fees already included in other approvals. These figures are government fees only and exclude architect, expediter, and construction costs. The outdoor dining cases at 1650 Haight St took 128 days (CUA filed Sept 2007, approved Jan 2008) plus 12 days for the variance, and at 1640 Haight St took 36 days (agency referral filed April 2013, approved May 2013), showing the wide range depending on the permit path.

records_summary: 1801 Haight St is an existing restaurant with an active ABC Type 47 license (full bar) that has operated continuously since at least 1992. The address is zoned NCD-HAIGHT where restaurants are principally permitted on the first story, but it sits within the Haight Street Alcohol Restricted Use Subdistrict which requires Conditional Use for any new on-sale liquor establishment. The restaurant currently holds a Type 47 license issued in June 2024 following a complex license history including Type 41, Type 75, Type 06/74 craft distillery licenses. The immediate block is extremely dense: 19 food/drink businesses and 8 active on-sale ABC licenses within 500 ft, with five bars in that radius. Because the concept enlarges an existing restaurant that already holds a Type 47 license, it appears to be a continuation of use rather than establishing a new liquor establishment, consistent with Planning's 2024 interpretation for the current license.
